title: Directional rate and utilization boundaries
requirement: Accept minimum/maximum rates and 1/100 percent utilization; reject values immediately outside every boundary. Verify the effective rate never becomes zero.

title: Profile delay, MTU, and packet-percentage boundaries
requirement: Cover zero, maximum, and out-of-range latency, jitter, virtual MTU, loss, duplication, and reordering values.

title: Identifier and name validation
requirement: Reject blank, untrimmed, uppercase, and otherwise invalid profile IDs; reject blank rule IDs and profile names.

title: Configuration reference invariants
requirement: Reject duplicate profile IDs, duplicate rule IDs, custom profiles claiming built-in ownership, built-in ID collisions, and missing global, quick-add, or rule profile references.

title: Invalid destination corpus
requirement: Cover blank hosts, malformed DNS names, wildcard IP literals, malformed/bracket-mismatched IPv6, port 0/65536, Unicode normalization failures, and whitespace around wildcard targets.

title: Disabled domain rule fallback
requirement: A disabled exact or wildcard rule must be ignored, allowing the next eligible rule or global profile to apply.

title: Explicit domain bypass over a throttled global profile
requirement: A matching `No throttling` rule must pass through while unmatched destinations retain the global condition.

title: Complete precedence permutation
requirement: Exercise exact with port, exact without port, longest wildcard with port, longest wildcard without port, global, and no match in one deterministic table, including different declaration orders.

title: Apex and nested wildcard boundaries
requirement: Confirm `*.example.com` excludes the apex, includes deeper subdomains, and does not suffix-match `notexample.com`.

title: Packet-only profile activity
requirement: A profile containing only packet loss, duplication, or reordering must remain active for packet mapping without incorrectly shaping proxy payload as packet loss.

title: Room migration into current schema 32
requirement: Open representative databases from every supported upgrade origin, especially the schema where Network Conditions tables first appeared and versions 29, 30, and 31 into 32. Preserve valid settings, profiles, rules, semantic criteria, priorities, and indexes.

title: Fresh database versus migrated database equivalence
requirement: Both paths must expose equivalent defaults, constraints, indexes, and repository snapshots.

title: Atomic profile deletion protection
requirement: A profile referenced by the global selection or any enabled/disabled rule must not be deleted. A quick-add-only reference must be cleared safely when its profile is deleted, without exposing an invalid snapshot.

title: Reset persistence contract
requirement: Reset must disable shaping and clear the global selection while retaining saved custom profiles and domain rules across restart.

title: Corrupt row matrix
requirement: Fail closed for malformed profile values, invalid targets, duplicate IDs/targets, and missing references—not only a missing global profile. Surface a recoverable diagnostic without deleting unrelated valid data.

title: Concurrent repository writes
requirement: Concurrent enable, profile, and rule edits must serialize without lost updates or transient invalid snapshots.

title: Immutable snapshot emission
requirement: One logical transaction must not expose a configuration containing a rule before its referenced profile or after that profile has disappeared.

title: Built-in catalog evolution
requirement: Adding or changing versioned built-ins must not overwrite custom profiles or break persisted references on restart.

title: Interrupted write and reopen
requirement: Simulate cancellation or database close during an edit and confirm the next startup returns the previous or complete new transaction, never partial state.

title: Sustained 100 kbps transfer
requirement: Forward a sufficiently long stream and verify measured delivery remains within a documented tolerance around 100,000 bit/s after startup, with no multi-second catch-up burst.

title: Concurrent connection fairness
requirement: Multiple channels sharing one effective rule must share the aggregate budget without starvation or multiplying the configured rate.

title: HTTP/2 stream fairness
requirement: Concurrent child streams on one connection must share the applicable aggregate budget without blocking unrelated destinations or exceeding the limit.

title: Utilization percentage
requirement: Verify the effective rate and actual schedule at representative percentages, including rounding at the minimum rate.

title: Idle credit behavior
requirement: Long idle periods must not accumulate an unbounded token burst. The next payload should receive only the documented bounded startup allowance.

title: Very small and very large payloads
requirement: Cover one-byte units, virtual-MTU boundaries, large `ByteBuf` values, and `FileRegion` counts without overflow or negative delays.

title: Monotonic time extremes
requirement: Cover a clock near `Long.MAX_VALUE`, backward or repeated test-clock values, and duration arithmetic overflow with fail-safe behavior.

title: Rule budget isolation
requirement: Different rules and the global profile must not accidentally share a bucket; flows using the same effective rule must share it.

title: Fixed latency semantics
requirement: Prove first-byte and subsequent-unit delay semantics with a monotonic test clock. Latency must not compound incorrectly for each streaming chunk.

title: Deterministic jitter bounds
requirement: A fixed seed and sequence must reproduce the same values, every result must remain within the configured signed bound, and byte/frame order must remain intact.

title: Live latency and jitter edit
requirement: Queued work must be safely replanned and active flows must observe the new policy without duplicate or lost delivery.

title: Live offline and recovery
requirement: Switching an active stream to Offline and back must produce the documented failure/recovery behavior immediately without stale budget credit.

title: Timeout behavior
requirement: Verify whether the message remains pending, the promise outcome, channel state, cleanup, and recovery. The test must match the documented timeout contract rather than only checking that bytes were not counted.

title: Reset-flow behavior
requirement: The flow must close once, fail outstanding promises, release queued buffers, and update fault telemetry without double release.

title: Seeded proxy fault distribution
requirement: Over a fixed sequence, verify determinism and expected count/tolerance for intermediate probabilities—not only always-fail behavior.

title: Zero-byte protocol units
requirement: Headers, trailers, and control frames with no payload must preserve ordering and must not consume bandwidth bytes or become stuck behind a zero-byte queue entry.

title: Per-flow queue boundary
requirement: Exercise exactly 8 MiB, one byte below, and one byte above. Overflow must use the selected/documented fault behavior and release every reference-counted message.

title: Aggregate queue boundary
requirement: Exercise exactly 64 MiB across multiple flows and verify one flow cannot corrupt another flow's accounting on rejection.

title: Channel close before scheduled release
requirement: Cancelling an active flow must cancel timers, release every buffer once, fail promises, decrement active flows, and return queued bytes to zero.

title: Handler removal and application shutdown
requirement: Removing the handler or closing the proxy must unregister configuration listeners and leave no scheduled tasks, open flows, or retained payloads.

title: Replanning multiple queued items
requirement: Disable, rate edit, rule edit, and profile edit with multiple upload/download entries must preserve direction ordering and exact-once forwarding.

title: Queue rejection telemetry
requirement: Rejected work must not be counted as forwarded; queued, delayed, and fault counters must remain internally consistent.

title: Bidirectional interleaving
requirement: Upload and download queues must progress independently without corrupting direction-specific deadlines or counters.

title: Repeated enable/disable cycles
requirement: Rapid cycles must not duplicate listeners, timers, or releases and must converge to the latest configuration.

title: HTTP/1.1 streaming matrix
requirement: Cover request upload, response download, chunked bodies, trailers, keep-alive reuse, redirects, byte ranges, progressive downloads, and cancellation.

title: HTTP/2 matrix
requirement: Cover concurrent streams, flow-control/backpressure, reset/cancel, trailers, streaming bodies, and aggregate fairness.

title: WebSocket matrix
requirement: Cover text, binary, fragmented messages, ping/pong, close frames, long-lived live edits, and exact ordering.

title: GraphQL WebSocket matrix
requirement: Cover connection setup, subscribe, next/error/complete, multiplexed operations, cancellation, and long-lived policy changes.

title: gRPC matrix
requirement: Cover unary, client streaming, server streaming, bidirectional streaming, trailers, cancellation, and uncorrupted framing.

title: SSE matrix
requirement: Cover incremental events, comments, reconnect, long idle gaps, cancellation, and absence of whole-body buffering.

title: CONNECT/TLS and opaque tunnel matrix
requirement: Cover authority parsing, IPv4/IPv6, early close, bidirectional traffic, TLS passthrough, applied evidence, and aggregate sharing.

title: API Studio conditions-only routing
requirement: When capture is paused but Network Conditions is enabled, HTTP, WebSocket, GraphQL WebSocket, and gRPC execution must use the local proxy and receive the selected condition.

title: API Studio unavailable proxy
requirement: If conditions are enabled but the proxy is stopped or unavailable, return an explicit safe error or documented fallback; never silently claim the condition was applied.

title: Paired-device proxied traffic
requirement: Eligible paired traffic must use the same rule policy and applied evidence as desktop captured traffic.

title: Control-plane exclusion
requirement: Pairing, certificate retrieval, condition-policy fetch, discovery, and the disable path must remain reachable and unthrottled.

title: No double shaping
requirement: Traffic already shaped in the proxy must bypass packet-level shaping, so 100 kbps does not become an effective 50 kbps or worse.

title: Destination continuity after upgrade
requirement: WebSocket and opaque upgraded flows must retain the validated destination and effective rule for their entire lifetime.

title: Unknown destination
requirement: Traffic without a trustworthy host/port must pass through with explicit unavailable evidence rather than matching display text or a stale previous destination.

title: Missing exchange result
requirement: A removed or unknown Traffic ID must produce the defined unavailable state and must not open an empty editor.

title: Opaque-flow quick-add
requirement: Valid protected/opaque flow destination metadata must prefill exact host and port; absent or untrusted metadata must disable the action.

title: Default and explicit ports
requirement: HTTP, HTTPS, IPv4, bracketed IPv6, and explicit non-default ports must produce the correct canonical target.

title: Existing disabled rule
requirement: Quick-add must open the existing equivalent rule without creating a duplicate or silently enabling it.

title: Navigation and prefill integration
requirement: The Traffic action must navigate once, preserve the selected transaction, and open the fully prefilled Network Conditions editor.

title: Action availability and reason

title: Applied evidence matrix

title: Live edit evidence

title: Sensitive-data boundary

title: Master enable and disable

title: Global profile selection

title: Reset action

title: Complete rule CRUD

title: Error recovery

title: Active-flow exactness
